title: Flow Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: Sundance spa's flow switch is not detecting water flow during heating.
fullDescription:
FL1 appears when the flow switch remains open while the circulation pump is running. The heater shuts off to prevent dry firing.

Dirty filters, low water level, airlock, or a failed flow switch itself are the typical causes. A restricted skimmer weir also prevents full flow.

Most owners can resolve FL1 by cleaning filters and purging airlock from the pump.
symptoms: Pump runs but no flow at jets

fixSteps.title: Clean filters
fixSteps.instruction: Remove filter cartridges, hose them down thoroughly. Replace annually.

fixSteps.title: Purge airlock
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen pump union slightly until water hisses out, retighten.

whenToCallPro: Circulation pump replacement requires a spa tech.
videoSearchQuery: Sundance spa FL1 flow error fix

faq.a: No — it prevents dry-firing the heater element.

title: Flow Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: Flow switch is reading closed when the pump is off.
fullDescription:
FL2 indicates the flow switch is stuck closed — it reports flow even when the pump is not running. This is the opposite of FL1 and typically means debris or scale holds the paddle permanently tripped.

Some flow switch failures can even cause heater cycling. Replacement is a 20-minute job for a DIYer comfortable with plumbing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect switch
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off spa, close slice valves, remove flow switch and inspect paddle.

whenToCallPro: If plumbing unions are seized, call a tech.
videoSearchQuery: Sundance spa FL2 flow switch replacement

faq.a: Only if slice valves don't fully close.

title: Water Overheat Shutdown
shortDescription: Water temperature exceeded 112°F — spa shut down for safety.
fullDescription:
OH means the spa detected water above 112°F and shut down heating. Sundance spas usually also disable pumps until temperature drops below a safe threshold.

Caused by stuck heater relay, dirty filters forcing long pump cycles, or high ambient heat with spa cover closed. Open the cover and let it cool.

causes.cause: Long pump runtime from dirty filters

symptoms: Water steams when cover is opened

fixSteps.title: Open cover
fixSteps.instruction: Remove spa cover, let water cool to below 100°F (usually 30-90 minutes).

faq.a: Usually not — the shutdown protects the equipment.

title: High Limit Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The high-limit temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
SN1 on Sundance spas refers to the high-limit sensor in the heater housing. Open, shorted, or disconnected sensor will trigger this code.

Replacement sensors are inexpensive and plug directly into the control pack with a 3-pin connector.

fixSteps.title: Reseat sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Open control pack, reseat 3-pin sensor plug.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is in sealed heater tube, call a tech.

faq.a: High-limit — mounted in the heater tube.

title: Temperature Sensor 2 Fault
shortDescription: The water temperature sensor (regulation sensor) is out of range.
fullDescription:
SN2 points to the regulation sensor. Without it, the control cannot maintain setpoint and will disable heat.

Test resistance — typical value is ~10-30kΩ at room temperature. Replace if reading is open or shorted.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug sensor, measure ohms; replace if out of spec.

whenToCallPro: Stuck sensor in tee requires pro.

faq.a: Aftermarket usually works fine; Balboa pn can substitute on 880 series.

title: Dry Fire Protection
shortDescription: Heater may be running dry — spa shut down for safety.
fullDescription:
DR indicates the high-limit reached temperature too quickly, suggesting the heater element might be running without water. Most commonly happens after a fill-up when air is still trapped.

Purge air from plumbing and restart. If DR returns, inspect heater element and flow path.
symptoms: Spa shuts down right after fill

fixSteps.title: Purge air
fixSteps.instruction: Run jets in short 10-second bursts to clear trapped air.

whenToCallPro: If DR persists with full water, call a tech.
videoSearchQuery: Sundance spa DR dry fire error

faq.a: Yes — purging air fixes most DR codes post-refill.

title: High Limit Trip
shortDescription: High-limit safety tripped at 118°F — spa locked out.
fullDescription:
HL code means the high-limit sensor tripped to protect components. Unlike OH (which often self-resets), HL typically requires a manual reset via the control panel.

Check filters and heater for scale buildup. Recurring HL usually means scale is insulating the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Cool and reset
fixSteps.instruction: Allow spa to cool to below 100°F and reset via panel.

videoSearchQuery: Sundance spa HL high limit fix

faq.a: Possible with diluted spa-safe descaler but follow manufacturer directions.

title: Freeze Protection Active
shortDescription: Cold water detected — freeze protection running pumps.
fullDescription:
The ICE message (sometimes abbreviated as a snowflake icon) is informational — it indicates Sundance is running pumps intermittently to prevent pipe freezing. This is not an error.

If ICE persists in warm weather, the freeze sensor may be miscalibrated.

fixSteps.title: No action needed
fixSteps.instruction: Let freeze protection run — spa will resume normal mode when warmer.

whenToCallPro: Only if ICE appears in warm weather.

faq.a: No — protecting plumbing from freeze damage.

title: Pump Overload
shortDescription: A pump motor drew too much current — overload trip.
fullDescription:
OE indicates a motor has exceeded current limits. Seized bearings, blocked impeller, or electrical issues cause this.

Power cycle to clear. If OE returns, identify the affected pump and inspect.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off spa breaker 2 minutes, restart.

faq.a: Usually OE1/OE2 denote pump number; consult topside menu.

title: Water Below Setpoint
shortDescription: Water is more than 20°F below setpoint — informational message.
fullDescription:
COOL is not a fault — it informs you water is significantly below desired temperature. Appears after refilling or extended power loss.

Heater runs until setpoint is reached and COOL clears automatically.

fixSteps.title: Wait for heat-up
fixSteps.instruction: Let spa heat normally — takes 4-24 hours depending on starting temp.

whenToCallPro: If COOL lingers after 24 hours, heater isn't working — call tech.
